title: The Rice Threshers
description: Taguig takes its name from 'taga-giik', the rice threshers who farmed its lowlands. Spanish speakers pronounced it 'tagui-ig', later shortened to Taguig.

title: City on the Lake
description: Taguig has more than 10 kilometers of shoreline on Laguna de Bay, the country's largest lake, where traditional fishing communities remain active.

title: From Fort to Financial Hub
description: The former Fort William McKinley, later Fort Bonifacio, is now Bonifacio Global City, home to the Philippine Stock Exchange, embassies, and major businesses.

title: Heritage Landmarks
description: The Napindan Lighthouse in Tipas, once a meeting point of revolutionaries, and the Minor Basilica of Saint Anne, the city's main church, anchor its history.
